title: Safer hand — choose the visual world
question: Three grounded directions from the conventional end, shaped by your steer: premium, modern, product-focused — no neon, no terminal, no glassmorphism. Pick one, take the category standard, or steer further.

options.label: The API Reference
options.lineage: OpenAPI documentation: endpoints, methods, request and response
options.thesis: Your portfolio as the reference documentation of a system you built — every project an endpoint, every case study a response body, filters as method chips.
options.viewport: A documentation masthead: your name as the package name, role as the tagline, projects listed as endpoint entries — each with a method chip, path, and one-line description — and the featured project carrying the only "200 OK" badge.
options.risk: Docs aesthetics are a known developer move; it wins only with real product depth and a committed visual system, never a theme.

options.label: The Editorial Portfolio
options.thesis: Projects as editorial features: a cover line, a lede, a spread — case studies with the gravity of a designed publication.
options.viewport: A masthead hero with a cover line for the featured project; below, projects index as a spread grid of editorial headlines over generous white space.
options.risk: Editorial is the default register for "premium"; without a strong voice it reads as a generic magazine.

options.label: The Technical Spec Sheet
options.lineage: engineered product datasheets and instrument catalogs
options.thesis: Every project as a precision spec sheet: measured tables, hairlines, and a featured datasheet you can unfold.
options.viewport: A datasheet hero: the featured project as a full spec sheet with a callout to its architecture; the rest index as a catalog of concise spec entries.
options.risk: Technical precision can read cold or corporate; warmth must come from the copy and real screenshots.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: The clean premium portfolio this category ships at its best — refined hero, strong project grid, tech tags — executed impeccably.
options.viewport: A calm hero with name and role, a filterable project grid, a career timeline, and a contact bar — the arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
options.case: Played against the dark-neon typewriter hero, the stock card-grid template, and the glassy awwwards look — the straight version of this category, at full fidelity.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
